There are times when I barely sleep but feel totally wired, like I can work straight through the night grooming dogs and still have energy to clean the whole house. My mind races, and I talk so fast my coworkers have actually asked if I’m okay. That’s happened a few times in the past year—each time lasting about four or five days.  

During those spells, I get this urge to eat constantly. I’ll go through entire bags of chips or finish a family-sized pizza alone in my car, even when I’m not hungry. It’s embarrassing, so I don’t do it around people—usually hide in my car after work and just… consume. I keep eating until I feel sick, but I can’t seem to stop.  

But then it all crashes. I feel guilty, exhausted, and won’t leave my apartment for days. The thing is, those hyper times aren’t just about food—they come with this intense energy, like my brain’s on overdrive. I know it’s more than just bingeing because the moods come with it, and they’re not normal. That pattern’s happened more than once, and my therapist said it might be more than just eating issues.
D023-D009_h023.options:
A. Bipolar II Disorder
    B. Binge-Eating Disorder
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Adjustment Disorder

D023-D009_h024.question:
There are times—usually a few days every couple months—when I feel like I’m running on overdrive. I get these bursts where I’m super productive, barely sleeping, and my ideas for content just won’t stop. I’ll post constantly, pitch three campaigns in one night, and feel like I’m finally “in the zone.” But when that energy crashes, I fall into these heavy lows.  

Then there are the eating episodes. I don’t know how else to explain it—suddenly, I’ll eat an entire pizza or a family-size bag of chips in one sitting. I’m not even that hungry, but it’s like something takes over. I keep going until I feel sick, and I always do it alone because I’m so ashamed. I’ve canceled plans just to binge in private.  

These binges happen mostly when I’m not hyped up. The thing is, those intense high-energy phases? They’re not just motivation—they last at least four days, I’m more impulsive, spend too much online, and coworkers have asked if I’m okay. I’ve never lost control like this for weeks, but the pattern is clear: short highs, deep lows, and this eating shame in between. It’s not *just* about food—it’s part of the bigger cycle.
D023-D009_h024.options:
A. Bipolar II Disorder
    B. Binge-Eating Disorder
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Adjustment Disorder

D023-D009_h025.question:
I’ve been having these episodes where I eat so much in one sitting—way more than anyone should, like an entire box of pastries or multiple dinners back-to-back. It happens mostly at night after work, when I’m alone. I keep eating even after I’m painfully full, and I feel so ashamed I’d never do it in front of anyone. My husband doesn’t really know; I wait until he’s asleep.  

But it’s not just the eating. There are times—usually a few days at a stretch—where I feel wired, like I don’t need much sleep and still have tons of energy. I talk fast, jump from idea to idea, and take on big projects, like rearranging our entire budget or starting three new workout plans at once. I feel *on*, like I can handle anything. But then it crashes—into sadness, exhaustion, and I retreat.  

This pattern’s been going on for years, with episodes every few months. The eating feels tied to it—worse during those high-energy phases. My job’s stressful, but during those times, I actually feel sharper, more confident. Still, I know it’s not sustainable. I’ve had these mood swings long before the bingeing became a problem, and they’re too intense to ignore.
D023-D009_h025.options:
A. Bipolar II Disorder
    B. Binge-Eating Disorder
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Adjustment Disorder
